rationale: Fresh center penalty preserves the parent's Boolean function: an empty center requires at least three occupied cardinal neighbors; an occupied center always yields zero. Supplied parent evidence already solves 40/40 development cases, so no strict development gain is claimed.

Positive rescaling by one half gives fresh literal parameters with exactly the parent's step output on every input. Supplied parent evidence already solves 40/40 development cases; this preserves performance without claiming strict development gain.

Reducing the empty-center coefficient and bias magnitude together preserves the three-neighbor threshold. An occupied center remains negative even with four occupied cardinal neighbors. This preserves the parent's function on the typed one-hot domain; its supplied 40/40 development result leaves no strict development gain available.
